title: A germ-compatible constant model on every strict-local fibre
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $\bar x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ be a geometric point [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks], and let $\bar t:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'\to S_{(f(\bar x))}$ be any geometric point. Write $T=X_{(\bar x)}$, $V=T\times_{S_{(f(\bar x))}}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega'$, $j:T\to X$ and $p:V\to T$ for the maps in [def-weil-pbc-local-acyclicity-abelian-sheaf]. For a locally constant abelian sheaf $G$ [def-constructible-locally-constant] [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], put $M=G_{\bar x}$. There is an isomorphism $e:\underline M_V\simeq (j\circ p)^*G$ such that the canonical map $\alpha_{G,\bar x,\bar t}:G_{\bar x}\to\Gamma(V,(j\circ p)^*G)$ equals the constant-section adjunction unit $M\to\Gamma(V,\underline M_V)$ [def-weil-pbc-global-sections-functor] followed by $\Gamma(V,e)$. No acyclicity or torsion assumption is needed.

proof.text: The chosen strict-local ring is strictly henselian local. Pull G back to T; pullback preserves local constancy. Choose a trivializing etale cover of T and a member with a point above its closed point. The etale-neighbourhood section theorem supplies a section of this member over T. Pulling its constant trivialization back along that section makes the sheaf F=j^*G constant. The composition and identity comparisons for inverse images identify this pullback with F.

Every etale cover of T has a split member. Consequently sheafification of a constant presheaf does not change its value at the terminal etale object: the unit of constant sheaf adjoint to terminal evaluation is bijective. Thus the constant-sheaf functor is fully faithful. Its counit C(Γ(T,F))→F is invertible because F is constant. This is implemented using the proved bijective_toSheafify_app theorem and the general fully-faithful-adjunction API, without choosing any coefficient object from an unproved existence statement.

The unique canonical germ restriction r:M→Γ(T,F) is an isomorphism. Define e₀:C(M)≅F to be C(r) followed by the counit. The adjunction triangle, equivalently homEquiv.apply_symm_apply, gives η_M followed by Γ(e₀) equal to r.

Pull e₀ back along p and compose with the inverse pullback-constant and inverse-image-composition comparisons to get e on V. For any coefficient N, the constant-section unit on T followed by pullback of sections and the pullback-constant isomorphism equals the unit on V. To verify this identity, transport sections to evaluation at the terminal etale object; the units under the right-adjoint uniqueness isomorphisms and then the left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism give exactly the two units. The sections pullback map is natural by naturality of the inverse-image adjunction unit. Apply this naturality to e₀, cancel the pullback-constant isomorphisms, and use the preceding equality η;Γ(e₀)=r. The resulting composite is r followed by pullback of sections and the inverse composition comparison, which is the defining localAcyclicityAlpha.

Use the general pointed-section-cone restriction on strictLocalSectionCone, the existing exact-sections instance for the small colimit model, and the general exact-global-sections Leray comparison wherever the former specialized restriction API was used. The cone restriction has the same section formulas, its germ predicate is definitionally identical, and uniqueness identifies the chosen stalk maps. All other argument steps and all scheme models stay as before.

For the unchanged small-colimit model, use the uniquely characterized residue equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-functoriality] to obtain its closed lift y over the original geometric point. The residue prime-comap formula puts y above the closed point. By [lem-weil-pbc-strictly-henselian-sections-stalk], the identity-neighbourhood germ is invertible. The residue factorization at every representative limit leg proves compatibility of y with strictLocalSectionCone. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-pointed-section-cone-stalk-iso] to the very same chosen restriction r. Only the proof of IsIso r changes; r, its characterization, and the resulting isomorphisms and source legs are unchanged.
